approved: Supported the Defence Trade Controls Amendment Bill 2015, arguing that it would strengthen Australia's export controls and meet international obligations while responding to stakeholder concerns. Reported that the bill would delay offence provisions by 12 months, create exceptions, streamline permits, narrow publication and brokering offences, and continue review of the legislation.

Summed up the Defence Trade Controls Amendment Bill 2015, which will let Defence focus on higher-risk non-physical transfers while handling lower-risk activities more efficiently; the amendments followed two years of stakeholder work led by the Strengthened Export Controls Steering Group.
